changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6238-object-payload-enabled.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` — edited by this change

  > **No published type changed.** `ObjectMetadataPayload` is exported from its module but that module is not re-exported by `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`, the package's only entry, so the removed `enabled?: boolean` was never on the published surface and no `**/src/index.ts` is touched. What consumers *can* observe is behaviour: `MetadataService` is reachable through the published `useMetadataService()` hook, both method signatures are unchanged (`PromiseANGLE-BRACKETS(void)`), and the HTTP request they issue changes from a `PUT` with a body to a `DELETE`.

### `.changeset/6559-expression-user-input-contract.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` — edited by this change

  > WHAT BREAKS, AND FOR WHOM. This tightens a signature published from the package entry (`packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`), so an external caller that passes an unchecked or under-declared value stops compiling on upgrade. That is accepted (maintainer ruling 2026-08-27, option A): the only calls it refuses are calls that were never conformant with the contract the module already declared. It ships as `minor`, not `major` — objectui's major tracks `@objectstack`'s, so its own breaking changes ship as a minor with the break written down (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`). ⛔ Keeping `unknown` and ⛔ adding a second, wider entry point were both declined.

### `.changeset/7070-no-invented-gantt-date-fields.md`

- names `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — the console object page. The inline branch becomes `ganttViewOptions`, the sibling of `calendarViewOptions` and `timelineViewOptions`: the declared block spread whole, title floored at `'name'`, no date field invented. - `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — the render branch AND the capability gate. - `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `generateViewSchema`, the authored `object-view` element route, which bypasses `ListView` entirely.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `2049b03df` (merge-base with origin/main): 7 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1706 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2308 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36452595289)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f5cf7121d3662317ee6cd8791404c3949f0ea6b7`

### ① Derived judgments

**The interface matches the ruling.**
- `export interface ConsoleObjectViewProps` is in `views/ObjectView.tsx`. Its members match 5871194128 exactly:
  - `dataSource: DataSource`, required, imported as a type from `@object-ui/types`. That package is a runtime `dependencies` entry of app-shell, so the emitted `.d.ts` resolves for consumers.
  - `objects: any[]`, required.
  - `onEdit: (record: Record of string to unknown) => void`, required.
  - `externalRefreshKey?: number`.
- Both functions are typed with it. `ObjectViewInner` really is typed: its parameter is `ConsoleObjectViewProps`, not `any`.
- The type is exported only as a type: `export type { ConsoleObjectViewProps }` in `views/index.ts`, then added to the entry's existing `export type { … }` list beside `RecordFormPageProps`. There is no new runtime export, and `ObjectViewInner` stays unexported.
- plugin-view is untouched.
- The package `exports` map has only `.` and `./styles.css`. `RuntimePersistCtx` is not reachable from `.`, and the dev reports 0 hits in `dist/index.d.ts`. So the only change to the published `.d.ts` is `ObjectView`'s parameter type and the new interface.

**The repairs are typing, not escape hatches.**
- **TS2722.** The fix is `dataSource.updateViewConfig?.(…)`. The guard `if (!dataSource?.updateViewConfig …) return` reads the same captured `dataSource` binding that the 300 ms closure calls. The new no-op path (where it used to throw) can only happen if an adapter loses its method inside the debounce window. The behaviour is preserved in practice, and this does not need its own disclosure.
- **The two TS2559s.** `(object & Partial OF ViewCacheInvalidator) | null` is truthful:
  - The seam's only use is `typeof ctx.dataSource?.invalidateViewKeys === 'function'` followed by `.call`.
  - All four callers pass something the new type admits: ObjectView (`DataSource`), ObjectDataPage (`any` props), ReportView (`DataSource` or undefined) and RuntimeDraftBar (`any`).
  - The intersection still refuses a primitive and a wrongly typed `invalidateViewKeys`.
- There is no `as any` and no `@ts-expect-error` in source.

**Callers are fine.** App-shell's `ObjectView` has exactly two mounts, both in app-shell's own `console/AppContent.tsx`. Both pass all four props, and `handleEdit` is `(record: any)`. `examples/byo-backend-console` mounts plugin-view's `ObjectView`. No caller needed a change, and none relied on `any` for something the interface refuses.

**Ratchet edit (`overlayPatchOnly`): not weakened.** `ObjectView.tsx` has one `updateViewConfig` call site. The pattern still requires `buildPersistedViewBody(` in the call body and refuses the `...baseViewDef` spread, and its vacuous-pass guard is unchanged. The `unboundAdapterCall` ratchet is not affected by the change.

**BLOCKING 1 — the pin does not bind the ruled optionality of `onEdit` or `objects`, or the TS2739 it claims.**
- `@ts-expect-error` is satisfied by any error, whatever its code. The mount `ObjectView dataSource={DATA_SOURCE}` errors whenever EITHER member is required.
- Two mutations stay green, with every other assertion still green:
  - `onEdit?:` (the exact alternative 5871194128 priced and rejected, "REQUIRED … optional costs 2");
  - `objects?:`.
  - Under either one, the line becomes TS2741, which consumes the directive. `_ParamIsTheDeclaredProps` compares the interface with itself, and the control still compiles.
- The `dataSourceX` row replaces `dataSource`, so an index signature added to the interface would also leave it green, through TS2741 on the missing `dataSource`.
- The value types of `onEdit`, `objects` and `externalRefreshKey` are not pinned at all. Only `dataSource` is (`_DataSourceIsTheContract`).
- The pin is red on base by construction (TS2305) and red under the `any` mutation, so those claims hold. It is simply not a pin of the ruled shape.
- **Required fix:** add to `ObjectView.consoleProps.types.test.tsx`:
  ```
  /** The ruled shape, member by member: names, optionality, value types (5871194128). */
  type _PropsAreTheRuledShape = Assert OF Equal OF (ConsoleObjectViewProps, {
    dataSource: DataSource;
    objects: any[];
    onEdit: (record: Record OF (string, unknown)) => void;
    externalRefreshKey?: number;
  })
  ```
  Write it in real generic syntax. Quote a red leg with `onEdit?:` (TS2344 on this line) and then green at head.

**Gap: `ObjectViewInner` cannot be reached by the pin.** Reverting only the inner parameter to `any` would stay green. The gap is disclosed in the PR's Acceptance notes and in the dev report's deviations. It is acceptable: the function is unexported and the ruling did not require pinning it.

**BLOCKING 2 — one changeset sentence is false.** The sentence is "A mount that passes the four props the component always read compiles as before." `onEdit` is a function-typed property, so `strictFunctionTypes` checks it contravariantly. A consumer handler typed `(record: Account) => void`, where `Account` has required fields, is now refused (TS2322). The same goes for a non-number `externalRefreshKey`. **Replacement:**
Replacement: A mount that passes the four props with values of the declared types compiles as before. An `onEdit` handler whose parameter is a narrower record type (for example an interface with required fields) is now refused under `strictFunctionTypes` and must accept `Record<string, unknown>`, and `externalRefreshKey` must be a number.

**Non-blocking wording.** The changeset's "Nothing changes at runtime." overstates slightly: the `?.` is a runtime byte, though it sits behind an existing guard. Suggested: "Nothing observable changes at runtime; the one runtime byte is an optional call behind an existing guard." The PR body already says this accurately.

**README.** Every sentence was checked against the source:
- the `objects.find` resolution and the "object not found" state;
- `externalRefreshKey` summed into `refreshKey`;
- `onEdit` called with the record.

The block is compiled by `check:doc-snippets`, and the dev's ablation shows it bites.

**Out of diff, non-blocking (follow-up).** The customer-published `skills/objectui/guides/project-setup.md` imports `ObjectView` from `@object-ui/app-shell` and mounts `ObjectView objectName="contact"` with no router. This is the card's own defect class: `objectName` is not a prop, and the three required props are missing. The mount was already broken at runtime on base and now fails to compile. No gate covers `skills/objectui/**`. Recommend filing it on the card rather than widening this PR.

### ② Semver level

`'@object-ui/app-shell': minor` is correct, and `Clause-②: yes` is right.
- The change adds a new exported type name.
- It narrows a published parameter from `any`. The narrowing is spelled out in the changeset body, per the fixed-group rule in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (objectui's major is pinned to `@objectstack`'s; breaks ship as `minor` with the body spelling them out).
- The nearest precedents (the SchemaRenderer and DashboardRenderer/ListView props-erasure repairs) landed as `patch`, but they restored an already-declared interface and added no export, so they do not argue for a lower level here.
- Not `major`. `Changeset Bump Policy` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are success.
- `Changeset Declaration` is success.

### ③ Boundary flags

**CI on the head** (42 check runs):
- **Required, success:** Lint, Type Check, Build & E2E, Build Docs, Changeset Declaration, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec Main Shape Gate, and Test shards 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 of 8.
- **Pending:** Test (shard 4/8) was still in progress at 16:36Z. That is not final; re-check before landing.
- **Test (dist pins):** success.
- **All other checks:** success, except these:
  - skipped: Test (coverage), the coverage shards and dependabot;
  - `Bundle Analysis`: failure, expected (below).
- **`Bundle Analysis`** is not required. Its report shows an eager closure of 3104.5 KB against a 3104.5 KB budget, with "Aggregate closure ceiling ❌ over its ceiling" and every other half ✅. That is the pre-existing overage on main tracked on objectui#10996. CI's KB rounding cannot isolate the PR's own delta. The dev's byte-level reading (3,179,020 on base, 3,179,021 at head, +1 gzip byte for the `?.`) is consistent with that report and is not this PR's failure.

**Merging:**
- `git merge-tree --write-tree` against current main `2049b03df7` is clean (tree `332eb5d6d2`). The 4 commits main gained since base `8aa68b1596` touch none of the PR's files. GitHub reports `mergeable_state` `behind`.
- Against PR objectui#10990's head `d3747ac005`, the one other open PR on these files (it touches `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`), merge-tree is also clean.

**Governance and PR state:**
- `check-governed-merges`: 0 of 8 paths governed, "NOT governed"; 221 changed lines, under the human-merge threshold.
- The PR is a draft, the assignee is `os-elon-musk`, and `needs:contract-review` is applied.

**Dispatch record:**
- The claim 5873302545 is the earliest live claim; 5828070713 is spent per the ruling.
- Both rulings and the claim are carried on the `Ruling-ref:` line.
- Deviations are disclosed in the PR body and in the newest `os-dev-report` 5874218979:
  - the pin is `.tsx` rather than `.ts`, justified by the JSX mounts and the `InspectorComboField.naming.types.test.tsx` precedent;
